newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish EMU decision Friday or June 18 - party.
newsitem.headline: Swedish EMU decision Friday or June 18 - party.

text.p: A committee of Sweden's ruling Social Democratic Party formed to rule on Swedish adhesion to the EU's Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) will take its decision this Friday or on June 18, a party official said on Tuesday.
Enn Kokk, secretary to the committee, told Reuters the decision had to be made before a party meeting on June 23.
"We have to have our view ready before the board of the Social Democratic Party meets in Skelleftea on June 23-24. The VU (committee) only meets twice before then," said Kokk.
Finance Minister Erik Asbrink has pledged to make Sweden's view of EMU membership clear in the next few weeks, ending a long period of speculation about whether Sweden will join or not.
Asbrink's spokeswoman said the minister would advise markets "in good time" before he announces his decision.
"I can't tell you what "good time" is but it would be at least a few hours before publication," Maja Nilsson told Reuters.
The meeting of the party committee (VU) will be held from 1000 to 1600 (0800 to 1400 GMT) on Friday. "If there is a decision you could expect publication after 1600," said Kokk.

The VU consists of Prime Minister Goran Persson, Foreign Minister Lena Hjelm-Wallen, Social Democratic Party secretary Ingela Thalen, former deputy Prime Minister Mona Sahlin, Parliamentary Party Chairman Sven Hulterstrom, Environment Minister Anne Lindh and Bertil Jonsson, head of the Swedish Trade Union Federation (LO).
Asbrink attends the meetings but does not have voting rights. -- Peter Fellman 08-700 1007
